step1_summary: Chief complaint: Lower abdominal (below umbilicus) pain, burning quality, getting worse over 2 days.

Symptoms: Gradual onset, constant lower abdominal pain (burning), worse with palpation, aware all the time but still functional; mild nausea; feeling hot and sweaty; increased urinary frequency; urine noted to be pink in color; no burning/stinging urination; constipation recently, now resolved; no vomiting, no diarrhea, no chest or breathing symptoms.
Past medical history: No surgical history, no chronic illnesses mentioned.
Medications/allergies: Only on contraceptive implant (Implanon) for 1 year; no other meds/allergies.
Family/social history: No family history of GI or relevant conditions; lives in a share house; works as accountant; no smoking; social alcohol.

Gynecological/sexual history: Sexually active with single partner (last intercourse 4 days ago), last STD screen 6 months ago (normal), on Implanon, last period 2 weeks ago, still gets periods, not using additional barrier contraception, does not suspect pregnancy but not formally ruled out.

V: Renal/ureteric stone: Pink urine suggests hematuria; pain could be referred to lower abdomen; however, no colicky pain or radiating pain described.
Interstitial cystitis: Lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency possible; less likely with acute onset.
I: Urinary tract infection (cystitis/lower UTI): Acute lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, pink urine, low grade fever (hot/sweaty), mild nausea.
Early pyelonephritis: Mild systemic signs, but lacks flank pain/major systemic illness.
Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID): Lower abdominal pain, recent sexual activity, low-grade systemic symptoms.
N: Bladder tumor: Pink urine possible, but unlikely in young woman with acute symptoms and no risk factors.
Gynecologic neoplasm: Same as above—unlikely with acute presentation.
I2: Implanon side effect: Unlikely, but minimal hematuria/abdominal pain could rarely be related.
Drug-induced cystitis (if any recent medications, though none reported).
C: Congenital urinary tract abnormality: Only relevant if this is a recurrent pattern, not reported.
A: Interstitial cystitis (as above): Lower abdominal pain/urinary frequency possible—unlikely acute.
E: Pregnancy complications (early miscarriage, ectopic): Sexually active, on Implanon, but low suspicion; timing of last period would be unusual for ectopic pain.
Diabetic cystopathy: No evidence of diabetes.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic presentation of lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, new hematuria (pink urine), systemic symptoms (hot/sweaty), mild nausea. No severe pyelonephritis features.
supporting_evidence: Recent constipation resolved (UTIs can be associated with these patterns)
opposing_evidence: No dysuria or suprapubic tenderness (though some UTIs present without dysuria)
